questions.question: 1. Which of the following is an array that does NOT have all elements of the same type?

explanations.a: Incorrect. All the elements are integers.
explanations.b: Correct. This array contains both strings and a boolean value, so not all elements are of the same type.
explanations.c: Incorrect. All the elements are strings.
explanations.d: Incorrect. All the elements are boolean values.

questions.question: 2. Which of the following arrays is sorted in descending order?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The numbers do not decrease from left to right; -8 is greater than -14 and -17, so the order is not descending.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This array is in ascending order, not descending.
explanations.c: Incorrect. -1 is greater than -100, so the order is not descending.
explanations.d: Correct. The numbers decrease or stay the same from left to right, so this is descending order.

questions.question: 3. Consider the following arrays: A = [5, -5, 10, 1] and B = [0, 100, 1, 0]. Which of the following arrays shows all elements from both arrays combined and sorted in ascending order?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This just combines the two arrays without sorting.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This just combines the two arrays without sorting.
explanations.c: Incorrect. -5 should come before 0, since -5 is the smallest value.
explanations.d: Correct. All elements from both arrays are present and sorted in ascending order.

questions.question: 4. If you repeatedly split an array into a fixed number of smaller parts at each step, how does increasing the number of parts you split into at each step affect the total number of splitting rounds needed to break the array down? (Assume you always split into the same number of parts at each round.)

answers.a: The number of rounds does not change; it is independent of the number of parts per step.
answers.c: The number of rounds decreases as you increase the number of parts per step.
answers.d: The number of rounds increases as you increase the number of parts per step.

explanations.a: Incorrect. The number of rounds does change depending on how many parts you split into each time.
explanations.b: Incorrect. There is a clear relationship: more parts per step means fewer rounds are needed.
explanations.c: Correct. If you split into more parts each time, you reach the smallest pieces faster, so fewer rounds are needed.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Increasing the number of parts per step actually reduces the number of rounds needed.
